summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Route-exposure design maps Nepal's third-country imports through Indian gateway ports (Kolkata/Haldia, Visakhapatnam) to the maritime chokepoints on their origin lanes (Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Malacca, Cape route), plus indirect petroleum exposure via Indian crude sourcing and aviation exposure via Gulf hubs. Leads located: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2024 (chokepoint chapter) and 2025, the February 2024 'Navigating Troubled Waters' rapid assessment of the Red Sea disruption, three 2026 UNCTAD notes on the Strait of Hormuz disruption, the World Bank LPI 2023 report, and Nepal dry-port/transit documents. Freight shock history (Red Sea 2023-2024, Hormuz 2026) is pending retrieval of index series; no values were taken from snippets.

findings.claim: Q1: Chokepoints transited by Nepal's third-country imports routed via Indian ports - share of third-country import value/volume by origin region (Gulf, Europe/Mediterranean, East/Southeast Asia, Americas) mapped to chokepoints (Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Malacca/Singapore Strait, Cape route) and to Indian gateway (Kolkata/Haldia, Visakhapatnam).
findings.note: Requires customs imports by origin country (Nepal FY) excluding India and China-overland, and NITDB/ICD cargo by gateway port; chokepoint assignment by great-circle shipping lane is an assumption (19C-A1). Leads 19C-L09..L11, 16B L18.

findings.claim: Q1b: Petroleum route exposure - crude origin of Indian refinery supply to IOC (Hormuz dependence) as indirect exposure of NOC imports.
findings.note: Requires Indian crude import origin shares (calendar/Indian FY April-March - document conversion) and NOC supplier arrangement (16B SPOF-01).

findings.claim: Q2: Freight-rate response to past chokepoint disruptions - Red Sea/Suez 2023-2024 and Hormuz 2026 - measured by container spot indices (e.g. SCFI/Drewry WCI) and tanker indices (Baltic Dirty/Clean), plus war-risk premium changes.
findings.note: Retrieve RMT 2024 ch.3, RMT 2025, Navigating Troubled Waters and 2026 Hormuz notes (19C-L01..L07); record index base dates. No index values taken from snippets.

findings.claim: Q2b: Pass-through from ocean freight to Nepal's landed import costs (inland leg India->Nepal) - no Nepal-specific study located.
findings.note: Requires freight-forwarder or NITDB tariff data per TEU Kolkata-Birgunj, and LPI 2023 timeliness indicators.

findings.claim: Aviation-route exposure: share of Nepal's international seat capacity routed via Gulf hubs and disruption from airspace closures (MoFA reports suspension of regular Middle East-sector flights from late February 2026 - to verify).
findings.note: Requires CAAN international traffic by carrier/route (16B L39-L41) and MoFA flight press releases (19D-L02, 19D-L04); seat data licensed (OAG/IATA) - gap.

findings.claim: 19C-A1: Chokepoint assignment by origin region follows standard shipping lanes to east-coast Indian ports (Gulf origins via Hormuz; Europe/Mediterranean/Black Sea via Suez-Bab el-Mandeb or Cape; East Asia via Malacca); transshipment hubs (Colombo, Singapore) are recorded separately.
Ocean freight indices are calendar-year; Nepal import values are Nepal FY (mid-July) - no mixing without a documented monthly conversion.

data_gaps: Port-level split of Nepal's third-country cargo (Kolkata/Haldia vs Visakhapatnam) - NITDB/ICD statistics not located as a file (also 16B gap).
No Nepal-specific pass-through study from ocean freight/insurance to landed costs.
Proprietary freight indices (Drewry, SCFI, Baltic) may only be available via UNCTAD/World Bank reproductions.

WebSearch budget for the session was exhausted during r1 before all lead searches were completed; leads marked 'NOT confirmed by web search' use catalog base URLs or known primary domains and must be verified on fetch.

assumptions.text: Lane-based chokepoint assignment by origin region (see findings).
Freight shocks enter the model only via trade_costs on imports; they are not added to GDP directly.

challenges.text: X31 route data require the customs origin-by-gateway cross-tab; please include gateway port in the transit dataset request.
Tanker freight and war-risk premium spikes in 2026 should be modelled separately from crude price changes in fuel_prices, to avoid double counting.
SPOF-02 (Indian transit ports) should record the 2026 Kolkata-Biratnagar rail service and ECTS amendment (to verify from CBIC primary notification) as a partial diversification.

uncertainty: High. Route shares and freight shock magnitudes are pending. Lane-based chokepoint assignment is an assumption; transshipment obscures true routing. 2026 Hormuz evidence is lead-level only.

route_exposure.method: Customs imports by origin (Nepal FY) x NITDB gateway port x lane-based chokepoint assignment (19C-A1); report value shares and HHI; petroleum and aviation handled as separate sub-routes.

routes.description: Gulf origins -> Strait of Hormuz -> Arabian Sea -> east-coast Indian ports -> rail/road to Birgunj/Biratnagar
Europe/Mediterranean/Black Sea origins -> Suez -> Bab el-Mandeb (or Cape diversion) -> Kolkata/Haldia/Visakhapatnam
East/Southeast Asia origins -> Strait of Malacca/Singapore -> Bay of Bengal -> Kolkata/Haldia/Visakhapatnam
Air cargo and passengers via Gulf hubs (Doha, Dubai, Abu Dhabi) and Indian hubs
